1. `cor-number-of-solutions-of-a-binomial-congruence`, `[L3]` → `thm-linear-congruence-solvability-and-solution-count`

- Restatement claims: “A solvable congruence \(uy\equiv v\pmod f\) has exactly \(\gcd(u,f)\) solution classes modulo \(f\).”
- Target Statement says: “Let \(a,b\in\mathbb Z\) and \(n\ge1\)… When it is solvable, it has exactly \(d=\gcd(a,n)\) solution classes.” The hypothesis \(n\ge1\) was dropped.
- Counterexample: take \(f=0,u=2,v=0\). Congruence modulo \(0\) is equality, so \(2y\equiv0\pmod0\) has only \(y=0\), hence one solution class, while \(\gcd(2,0)=2\).
- No numbered step depends on the enlargement: step 3.1 uses \(f=\varphi(n)\ge1\). Nevertheless `[L3]` itself asserts a false unrestricted claim.
- Severity: `fatal`.

## Nonfatal findings

2. `thm-prime-subfield-classification`, `[L5]` → `def-field-homomorphism`

- Restatement claims: “A field homomorphism preserves addition, multiplication, and \(1\), and is injective.”
- Target Definition states only the three preservation laws, then defines an embedding as an injective field homomorphism. It does not define every field homomorphism to be injective.
- Steps 1.1 and 1.2 use automatic injectivity. The cited item’s later Remark supplies the standard kernel argument, so a reader closes this immediately, but `[L5]` is not a faithful restatement of the designated Definition.
- Severity: `nonfatal`.

3. `prop-the-underlying-set-functor-on-fields-has-no-left-adjoint`, `[F2]` → `def-field-homomorphism`

- Restatement adds: “and is automatically injective because its kernel is an ideal of a field and does not contain \(1_F\).”
- The target Definition states only operation and unit preservation; injectivity appears only as a derived Remark.
- Step 1.3 uses injectivity to prove exact preservation of characteristic. `[F2]` itself sketches the standard sub-30-second kernel argument.
- Severity: `nonfatal`.

4. `thm-simultaneous-diagonalisation-of-commuting-diagonalisable-endomorphisms`, `[L4]` → `def-linear-combination-and-span`

- Restatement claims: “The span of a subset is the smallest subspace containing it, and its elements are finite linear combinations.”
- Target Definition separately defines finite linear combinations and defines \(\operatorname{span}(S)\) as the intersection of all subspaces containing \(S\); it does not identify those two descriptions. Its Remark explicitly says that identification is proved in `lem-span-is-the-set-of-linear-combinations`.
- Step 1.2 depends on the added clause to reduce an arbitrary family to a finite subfamily.
- Severity: `nonfatal` — retargeting the fact to the published span lemma, or giving the standard one-line subspace argument, closes it within 30 seconds.

5. `thm-bessel-inequality-and-finite-parseval-identity`, `[L3]` → `def-linear-combination-and-span`

- Restatement claims: “A vector belongs to the span of a finite list exactly when it is a finite linear combination of its members.”
- The target Definition does not state this equivalence; the separate published lemma above does.
- Step 3.1 depends on it. Moreover, span membership alone does not directly make \(v\) equal to the particular vector \(p=\sum_i\langle v,e_i\rangle e_i\); the converse also needs the preceding orthogonality calculation or uniqueness of orthonormal coordinates.
- Severity: `nonfatal` — the missing argument is immediate: if \(v\) is in the span, then \(v-p\) is both in that span and orthogonal to every spanning vector, hence is zero.

Coverage: opened all 38 published target Statements/Definitions and checked all 81 listed citation edges, including every named fact and consuming step. Citing items were sampled at the prescribed facts and steps rather than read cover-to-cover. All target statement-provenance labels were checked; none is `ai-generated`. One edge changed during the pass—`thm-automorphisms-of-a-finite-rank-free-abelian-group` `[L2]` now faithfully quotes the definition and derives inverse homomorphicity inline—so I re-read its current disk text and counted it clean. Nothing was inaccessible. Findings: **1 fatal, 4 nonfatal**.
